Two corrections and the data you were missing. Your lllm_v2.man scored 6 of 21 on the
official judge, so the grid loads and runs — it is the behaviour that is wrong, not the layout.

CORRECTION 1: I told you earlier that a pipe running into ':' was a load error. That was WRONG;
please disregard it entirely. An LM-75 DISPLAY room is drawn with '+' corners, '=' horizontal
borders and ':' vertical borders — the display analogue of '-' and '|'. Pipes are supposed to
terminate on those glyphs. I confirmed this against two judge-accepted programs (plotter 20/20,
snake 17/17). Your original pipe routing was fine.

CORRECTION 2: my original prompt showed you `out=[]` for every case and truncated the inputs.
That was badly misleading — this is a DISPLAY problem, so the expected result is the `frames`,
which I never gave you. Here is the complete data, with full frames for the first five cases:

=== COMPLETE PUBLIC TEST DATA ===
The earlier version of this prompt showed truncated inputs and `out=[]`, which was
misleading: this is a DISPLAY problem, so the real expected result is `frames`.
Display is 16x16.
Below is the complete data: `in` is the exact value sequence delivered to the input room,
`frames` is the exact sequence of display frames your program must commit.
